info.title: Shell-Tunnel API
info.description: Ultra-lightweight remote shell gateway. Provides a cross-platform REST/WebSocket API for programmatic interaction with system shells.

tags.name: Filesystem
tags.description: List, read, write, and delete files. By default these reach whatever the account running the server reaches, and `path` is absolute (`C:/data/x.bin`, `/srv/deploy/x.bin`; either separator). Starting with --fs-root <dir> confines them to that directory, and `path` becomes relative to it. The startup banner names the effective scope.

get.description: Returns server health status. Does not require authentication.

Returns API version and status information.

Requires a valid token (no specific capability).

Returns a list of all active sessions.

Required capability: `session.read`.

post.description:
Creates a new shell session with optional configuration.

Required capability: `session.manage`.

get.description:
Returns the current status of a session.

Required capability: `session.read`.

delete.description:
Terminates and removes a session.

Required capability: `session.manage`.

post.description:
Executes a command in an existing session.

Required capability: `exec`.

Executes a command without creating a persistent session.

Required capability: `exec`.

get.description:
Establishes a WebSocket connection for real-time command streaming in a session.

Required capability: `exec`.

Establishes a WebSocket connection for one-shot command execution.

Required capability: `exec`.

Returns one page of a directory's contents. Paginated by an opaque path cursor rather than an offset, so a file added or removed mid-walk cannot invalidate a page already returned — an unpaginated listing would also exceed the relay's 8 MiB body ceiling on exactly the trees this endpoint exists to serve.

`HEAD` reaches this same route (axum serves it automatically for every `GET` route) with the same `fs.read` capability.

Required capability: `fs.read`.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Walk subdirectories too. Default false (one level only).

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: Set to `sha256` to include a content hash on every file entry in this page. Hashing is per page, never per tree, so a large recursive listing cannot outrun the relay's 120s request timeout. Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Resume point: the opaque `next_cursor` from the previous page. Echo it back verbatim; a hand-built value is refused with 400 `bad-cursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Clamped to [1, 10000] rather than refused; default 1000.

400.description: `bad-path` (malformed path), `not-a-directory` (path names a file; use `/api/v1/fs/stat`), or `bad-cursor` (cursor is not a value this endpoint produced).

403.description: `path-escapes-root` (only reachable when `--fs-root` confines the scope) or `unreadable` (directory could not be opened) — a JSON body in either case. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.read`.

get.description:
Returns one filesystem entry, file or directory — the same shape `list` reports, so a consumer can hold results from either in one type.

`HEAD` reaches this same route (axum serves it automatically for every `GET` route) with the same `fs.read` capability.

Required capability: `fs.read`.

403.description: `fs-not-enabled`, `path-escapes-root`, or `reserved-path` (path resolves into the upload staging directory) — a JSON body in every case. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.read`.

get.summary: Download a file, or a range of it
get.description:
Returns the whole file, or one byte range of it via `Range`. Supports resumable downloads without any client-side protocol beyond ordinary HTTP: `If-Range` compares against the returned `etag` and refuses to stitch a stale prefix onto a file that changed mid-transfer, falling back to the whole file (200) rather than serving mismatched bytes.

`HEAD` reaches this same route (axum serves it automatically) and reports identical status and headers with no body — same capability, `fs.read`.

Required capability: `fs.read`.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Single-range `bytes=<start>-<end>` (open-ended and suffix forms accepted). A syntactically invalid or multi-range spec is ignored, not refused — the whole file is served instead.

parameters.name: If-Range
parameters.description: An `etag` previously returned for this path. When it no longer matches, the `Range` is ignored and the whole file is served (200) rather than resuming onto a file that changed.

200.description: The whole file. Headers: `content-type: application/octet-stream`, `accept-ranges: bytes`, `etag`, `content-length`.

206.description: The requested byte range. Headers as for 200, plus `content-range: bytes <start>-<end>/<size>`.

400.description: `bad-path` (malformed path), or `not-a-file` (path is a directory or other non-regular entry; use `/api/v1/fs/list`).

403.description: `fs-not-enabled`, `path-escapes-root`, or `reserved-path` (path resolves into the upload staging directory) — a JSON body in every case. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.read`.

416.description: Range Not Satisfiable — a well-formed `bytes` range naming bytes the file does not currently have. Header: `content-range: bytes */<size>`.

delete.description:
Removes the named entry — a file, a symlink, or any other non-directory node — with no flags needed: `204`, no body, the same answer this route has always given. A *real* directory additionally needs `recursive=true`; without it the request is refused rather than acting on part of a tree the caller may not have meant to take whole. Add `dry_run=true` to preview a removal (real or recursive) instead of performing it — the same walk the removal itself uses, reporting counts without touching anything.

These flags guard against a caller's mistake, not against a caller: a token holding `fs.write` can already remove anything the server can reach, so this is not a permission boundary.

Required capability: `fs.write`.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Required to remove a real directory; without it, a directory target is refused with `400 recursive-required`. Has no effect on a file, symlink, or other non-directory node — those are always removed regardless of this flag.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Report what a removal would take instead of performing it. Same response body as a real removal, and nothing is removed either way.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Largest number of `entries` to report for a directory removal. Clamped to [1, 10000] rather than refused; default 1000. Only caps the listing — `removed` and `bytes` still cover the whole tree (`truncated` marks a longer list than this).

200.description: A directory removal or preview (`recursive=true`, with or without `dry_run=true`), or a preview of a single-entry removal (`dry_run=true` alone, `recursive` irrelevant). `removed`/`bytes` are exact only in this response — see the 500 responses for when they are a lower bound instead.

204.description: Removed. Only for an actual removal of a file, symlink, or other non-directory node — `dry_run` unset or `false`, the default and the backward-compatible case: a single-file delete with no flags at all behaves exactly as before this endpoint gained `recursive`/`dry_run`. A directory always answers 200 or an error instead, never this.

400.description: `bad-path`, or `recursive-required` (path is a real directory; pass `recursive=true` to remove it and everything under it).

403.description: `fs-not-enabled`, `path-escapes-root`, or `reserved-path` (path resolves into the upload staging directory) — a JSON body in every case. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.write`.

409.description: `staging-in-tree` — an upload is in flight somewhere under this directory. Refused whole rather than removed around it; cancel the upload or wait for it to finish, then retry.

500.description: For a plain removal: `delete-failed` (the OS refused it) or `delete-panicked` (unexpected failure). For a directory removal: `partial-delete` (some entries were removed, some were not) or, only under `dry_run=true`, `preview-incomplete` (some entries could not even be enumerated, so nothing was removed and the counts are a lower bound rather than exact). The last two share one body — the same fields as the 200 response plus `failures`, the paths that did not go — and are not interchangeable: reporting one as the other means reporting a deletion that never happened.

post.description:
Declares a destination, a total size, and a whole-file SHA-256, and opens a session to receive it in chunks. Nothing is written to the destination until `POST /api/v1/fs/uploads/{id}/complete` verifies the digest and renames the staged bytes into place atomically — a partial file never appears at the destination.

Required capability: `fs.write`.

400.description: `bad-path`, or `bad-digest` (`sha256` is not 64 lowercase hex characters).

403.description: `fs-not-enabled`, `path-escapes-root`, or `reserved-path` (destination resolves into the upload staging directory) — a JSON body in every case. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.write`.

409.description: `destination-busy` (another session already targets this path) or `destination-is-directory` (the destination already exists as a directory).

429.description: `too-many-uploads` — too many sessions are open; finish or cancel one and retry.

500.description: `io-error` (destination directory could not be created, or another OS failure), `path-resolution-failed` (defensive: the destination's canonical path could not be recomputed after `resolve_for_create` already accepted it), or `create-upload-failed` (unexpected failure). See 507 for the out-of-space case.

507.description: `io-error` — the destination's filesystem is out of space or quota (Unix `EDQUOT`; Windows quota reporting is tracked separately).

get.description:
Reports the next byte offset the server expects — where to resume an interrupted upload from. Reads only in-memory session state; never touches disk.

Required capability: `fs.write` (not `fs.read` — an upload session is a write operation end to end, including checking where it left off).

403.description: `fs-not-enabled` — a JSON body. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.write`.

patch.description:
Appends `chunk_size` (or fewer) bytes at the offset named by `Content-Range`. The offset must equal the session's current offset exactly — a chunk that arrives twice is refused by position, not silently re-appended.

Required capability: `fs.write`.

parameters.name: Content-Range
parameters.description: `bytes <start>-<end>/<total>`. Only `<start>` is consulted; the chunk's length is the request body's own length.

400.description: `bad-content-range` — the `Content-Range` header is missing or not of the form `bytes <start>-<end>/<total>`.

403.description: `fs-not-enabled` — a JSON body. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.write`.

409.description: `offset-mismatch` — the chunk does not continue from the session's current offset. `offset` in the body names the position to resend from.

413.description: `chunk-too-large` (this request body exceeds the advertised `chunk_size`) or `declared-size-exceeded` (this chunk, added to bytes already received, would exceed the `size` declared when the session was created).

500.description: `io-error` (write failed for a reason other than disk space) or `append-failed` (unexpected failure). See 507 for the out-of-space case.

507.description: `io-error` — the destination's filesystem is out of space or quota.

delete.description:
Cancels an in-progress upload and removes its staged bytes. As terminal for the audit trail as letting the session expire on its own — an explicit cancel is recorded the same way a sweep-driven expiry is, so the trail never shows a session starting with no matching end.

Required capability: `fs.write`.

403.description: `fs-not-enabled` — a JSON body. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.write`.

post.description:
Verifies the assembled bytes against the SHA-256 declared at session creation, then renames the staged file onto its destination atomically — the destination holds either the old file or the new one, never a half-written one.

Required capability: `fs.write`.

403.description: `fs-not-enabled` or `path-escapes-root` — a JSON body in both cases. Also reached, with an empty body, when the token lacks `fs.write`.

422.description: `checksum-mismatch` — the assembled bytes do not match the declared digest. The session is discarded; start a new one.

500.description: `io-error` (directory creation or rename failed for a reason other than disk space) or `complete-upload-failed` (unexpected failure). See 507 for the out-of-space case.

507.description: `io-error` — the destination's filesystem is out of space or quota.

bearerAuth.description: Opaque bearer token via the Authorization header. Each token carries a set of capabilities (exec, session.read, session.manage, fs.read, fs.write; '*' wildcard). A route declares a required capability: a missing/invalid token yields 401, a valid token lacking the capability yields 403. Role presets: operator (exec, session.read, session.manage, fs.read, fs.write); file-write (fs.read, fs.write); file-read (fs.read); full-control (*). The cut line is exec: a token holding it already reaches every file the server can, so operator carries the file capabilities too. The file-* presets carry no exec, and there the file capabilities are the whole grant.

uploadId.name: id
uploadId.description: Upload session identifier, returned as `upload_id` by `POST /api/v1/fs/uploads`.

shell.description: Shell command to use (e.g., bash, powershell.exe)

FsEntry.description: One filesystem entry, as reported by `stat` and by each `list` item — the same shape in both, so a consumer can hold results from either in one type.

size.description: Size in bytes. Zero for directories.

sha256.description: Content hash, present only when the caller asked for it (`list`'s `hash=sha256`; never on `stat`).

next_cursor.description: Opaque token to pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Absent on the last page.

DeleteResult.description: Body for the 200 responses from `DELETE /api/v1/fs/file`: a directory removal or preview (`recursive=true`, with or without `dry_run=true`), or a preview of a single non-directory entry (`dry_run=true` alone). `removed`/`bytes` are exact here; see `PartialDeleteResult` for when they are not.

removed.description: Entries counted (a preview) or removed (a real removal). For a directory this includes the directory itself; for a single non-directory entry this is always 1.

bytes.description: Total size of the files among those entries. Directories themselves contribute nothing.

entries.description: Root-relative paths of the entries counted, capped at the request's `limit` — see `truncated`.

truncated.description: `entries` stopped at `limit`. `removed` and `bytes` still cover the whole tree regardless.

dry_run.description: Echoes the request: `true` means nothing on disk was touched.

PartialDeleteResult.description: Body for the `partial-delete` and `preview-incomplete` 500 responses from `DELETE /api/v1/fs/file?recursive=true` — the same fields as `DeleteResult` plus `error` and `failures`. Unlike `DeleteResult`, `removed`/`bytes` here are not an exact count of what actually happened; see `error` for which condition produced this body and how the two differ.

removed.description: For `preview-incomplete`, a lower bound: an entry that could not be enumerated was never counted at all. For `partial-delete`, an entry whose removal itself then failed is still counted here — this is the number visited and attempted, not the number of entries actually gone. Either way, `failures` names what did not go.

bytes.description: Same caveat as `removed`, restricted to the files among those entries.

entries.description: Root-relative paths of the entries counted, capped at the request's `limit`.

failures.description: Root-relative paths that could not be removed (`partial-delete`) or could not even be enumerated (`preview-incomplete`).

error.description: `partial-delete`: a real removal where some entries survived. `preview-incomplete`: a `dry_run` that could not enumerate everything, so nothing was removed and the counts above are a lower bound rather than exact.

path.description: Destination. Absolute by default; relative to --fs-root when that flag confines the scope.

size.description: Total size the caller intends to send.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the whole file, 64 hexadecimal characters. Case-insensitive on input — the server normalises to lowercase before comparing at `complete`.

UploadState.description: A session's current state, returned by create, status, and each chunk append.

chunk_size.description: Largest chunk the caller may send, in bytes. Advertised rather than assumed, and always below the relay's 8 MiB body ceiling.

path.description: The destination the file was published to.

sha256.description: The verified digest — equal to the value declared when the session was created.

offset.description: The offset the session actually expects; resend the chunk from here.

expected.description: The sha256 declared when the session was created.

actual.description: The sha256 actually computed over the assembled bytes.

UnauthorizedError.description: Authentication required: the Authorization: Bearer token is missing or invalid (empty body).

ForbiddenError.description: The bearer token is valid but lacks the capability this route requires (empty body).
